company: Charter Hall Retail Management Limited (responsible entity of Charter Hall Retail REIT)
title: Securities Trading Policy for Directors and Employees

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of CHRML. Must provide prior notice of intention to deal to the Chairman (in addition to the general notification obligation), and must inform the Chairman and/or Company Secretary of any margin loans or similar arrangements taken over Securities.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Employees of Charter Hall, including contractors required to comply with Charter Hall's policies and procedures. Must notify the Chairman, an executive director of CHRML or the Company Secretary before dealing.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents, family members, companies or trusts used by a Director or Employee; the insider trading prohibition extends to Dealings conducted through them.

definitions.hedging_definition: The intention of this Policy is that it only permits hedging arrangements which are within the control of the Director or Employee rather than conferring control of any purchase or sale decision to a third party.

windows.end_anchor: day after public release to the ASX of CQR's estimated distribution for the half year ending 31 December
day after public release to the ASX of CQR's estimated distribution for the full year ending 30 June
day after public release to the ASX of CQR's half year results
day after public release to the ASX of CQR's full year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: CHRML may declare a Trading Blackout in respect of Securities at any time at its absolute discretion and without prior notice if considered necessary by the Directors; confidentiality of such a blackout is not addressed.

rules.detail: Securities is defined to include structured financial products, swaps, futures, CFDs, options, warrants, depositary receipts and other derivatives over or related to the performance of Securities, so dealing in derivatives is subject to the same notification and consent regime as any other Dealing, outside Trading Blackouts and while not in possession of Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Securities includes securities, debt securities and other financial instruments, issued by CQR or any interest created over Securities by third parties, structured financial products, swaps, future contracts, contracts for differences, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivates over or related to the performance of Securities.

rules.detail: Directors and Employees may only buy (go long) a derivative position, e.g. buying a put or call option, so that the hedge stays in their own control rather than a third party's, subject to the usual notification/consent, blackout and inside-information rules.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees are only permitted to buy a derivative position (for example this Policy permits entering into a contract to buy a put or a call option, however not a contract to sell a put or a call option).

rules.detail: Selling (writing) a put or call option is expressly excluded from the permitted hedging arrangements, whatever the security state.
rules.evidence: this Policy permits entering into a contract to buy a put or a call option, however not a contract to sell a put or a call option

rules.detail: Monetisation structures are not named. Securities includes 'any interest created over Securities by third parties' and Dealing includes agreeing to buy or sell, so a prepaid forward or similar monetisation is caught as a Dealing requiring notification and consent.
rules.evidence: Dealing includes: ... buying and selling; or agreeing to buy or sell

rules.detail: No express prohibition on short selling CQR Securities themselves (as distinct from the ban on writing/selling put or call options).
Securities lending is not named and is not captured by the Dealing definition (buy, sell, agree to buy or sell, procure, or communicate).

Contracts for differences are expressly listed within Securities. As a derivative, a CFD is only permitted long (bought), consistent with the section 3.4 ban on selling/writing derivative positions; a short CFD position is prohibited on that basis.
rules.evidence: structured financial products, swaps, future contracts, contracts for differences, options, warrants, depositary receipts or other derivates over or related to the performance of Securities

rules.detail: Margin loans over Securities are not prohibited and are not treated as a Dealing (no buy/sell/change of ownership) requiring prior consent; Directors must simply inform the Chairman and/or Company Secretary that the arrangement exists, and the Board decides whether market disclosure of the loan is required.
rules.evidence: Directors must also inform the Chairman and/or the Company Secretary of any 'margin loans' or similar arrangements taken by them over Securities. The Board of Directors will decide whether disclosure is required in relation to margin loans taken by Director/s.

rules.detail: No disclosure or clearance obligation is stated for Employees (as opposed to Directors) who take out margin loans.

Granting security over Securities under a margin loan or 'similar arrangement' is not prohibited; Directors must disclose it to the Chairman/Company Secretary, and it may be assessed by the Board for market price-sensitivity.
rules.evidence: Directors must also inform the Chairman and/or the Company Secretary of any 'margin loans' or similar arrangements taken by them over Securities.

rules.detail: Secured financing over Securities (margin loans 'or similar arrangements') is permitted for Directors subject only to post-arrangement disclosure to the Chairman/Company Secretary and Board consideration of ASX disclosure.
rules.evidence: Directors must also inform the Chairman and/or the Company Secretary of any 'margin loans' or similar arrangements taken by them over Securities.

rules.detail: The Policy does not address secured financing arrangements entered into by Employees.

Buying and disposing of Securities within four weeks or less of acquisition is contrary to the Policy, except where special leave for hardship or an entitlement-offer-related circumstance is obtained under section 5.2.
rules.evidence: It is contrary to this Policy for Directors and Employees to engage in short-term trading (ie buying Securities and disposing of them within four weeks or less form the date of acquisition) of Securities, except in the circumstances outlined in section 5.2 of this Policy.

clearance.approver: Chairman (notice of intention to deal); consent per section 5.2
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary and Chairman (or non-executive Directors if the Chairman is dealing)
clearance.evidence: In the case of a Director, they must also provide prior notice of any intention to Deal to the Chairman. ... Consent will not be given if there is any possibility that this Policy could be breached. No reason will be given for the grant or refusal of consent to Deal in Securities.

clearance.approver: Chairman, an executive director of CHRML, or the Company Secretary
clearance.evidence: all Employees Dealing in Securities must inform either the Chairman, an executive director of CHRML or the Company Secretary of any proposed Dealing not later than the day of the proposed Dealing

carve_outs: securities acquired as part of an entitlement offer
similar circumstances approved as special leave
short_term.evidence: buying Securities and disposing of them within four weeks or less form the date of acquisition

exceptions.approver: Managing Director(s) for staff; Chairman via the Company Secretary for a Director
exceptions.evidence: Leave will ordinarily only be granted in situations of financial hardship and only in the event that the person involved is not in possession of Inside Information affecting Securities.
Subsequent acquisitions of new Securities by virtue of the routine operation of the DRP need not be notified ... or consented to.
The restrictions in this Policy do not prevent a Director or an Employee from accepting a takeover bid or from selling Securities under a scheme of arrangement in respect of Charter Hall.

A situation may arise where Securities are held by Directors or Employees within a margin lending account and a sale of those Securities is enforced by the lending institution. If such a sale occurs during a Trading Blackout period, the Chairman will consider whether a breach of this policy has been made after considering all circumstances.

financing_disclosure: Directors: trigger = inception of a margin loan or similar arrangement; to whom = Chairman and/or Company Secretary; deadline = unspecified; the Board then decides whether ASX disclosure of the arrangement is required, noting margin loans may be price-sensitive information.

exemption_authority: Chairman and one of the Joint Managing Directors may grant special leave to deal within a Trading Blackout, ordinarily only for financial hardship and only if the person holds no Inside Information; confidentiality of a grant or refusal is not addressed for blackout leave, but general dealing consent refusals give no reasons.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees are only permitted to buy a derivative position ... however not a contract to sell a put or a call option.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The written-call leg of any collar cannot be granted by the executive under this Policy, which permits only long derivative positions; only the purchased-put leg is capable of being structured.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The intention of this Policy is that it only permits hedging arrangements which are within the control of the Director or Employee rather than conferring control of any purchase or sale decision to a third party.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a compliant long put must leave exercise/pricing decisions with the executive, not the bank counterparty, which may constrain how the bank structures settlement mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no equity plan or vesting provisions
bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to unvested securities, performance hurdles, employee equity incentive schemes or a minimum shareholding requirement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no vesting-based restriction on the shares to be collared, so the analysis turns entirely on the general dealing, hedging and short-term trading rules rather than any plan-specific lock-up.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board of Directors will decide whether disclosure is required in relation to margin loans taken by Director/s. ... in certain circumstances the existence of 'margin loans' or similar arrangements financing securities holdings may constitute material price sensitive information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A Director-level loan secured on the collared shares may trigger a Board assessment of whether the financing itself must be announced to the ASX.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If such a sale occurs during a Trading Blackout period, the Chairman will consider whether a breach of this policy has been made after considering all circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement of the bank's security over the collared shares during a blackout is not automatically excused; it is reviewed case by case for breach, creating execution uncertainty for the lender.

summary: A funded collar is only partially possible: Directors and Employees may buy (go long) a derivative position such as a put option under section 3.4, but the Policy expressly permits buying and not selling a put or call option, so the executive cannot write the call leg that funds the structure. Margin loans and 'similar arrangements' secured over Securities are not prohibited for Directors, who need only inform the Chairman and/or Company Secretary after the fact, with the Board deciding whether the financing itself must be disclosed to the ASX; the Policy is silent on secured financing by other Employees. Any dealing, including entering the put (and, if structured, the loan), must occur outside the four designated Trading Blackouts and any ad hoc blackout, with prior notification and consent from the Chairman/executive director/Company Secretary and no possession of Inside Information, and must not be short-term (held under four weeks) absent hardship or entitlement-offer circumstances. Enforcement of the bank's security through a forced sale during a blackout is not automatically permitted and is reviewed by the Chairman for breach. Overall, the loan and put-purchase legs are workable with notification, but the written-call leg as conventionally structured is not permitted under the express hedging clause.
